questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How Mozart became famous as a very young composer
Why so many great artists behave in strange ways
Whether artists' brains work differently from ours
How to teach children to play the piano at home
questions.why: Sam says the programme asks: are artists' brains different? They hear two expert opinions.

questions.q: What do Sam and Neil say about their own artistic abilities?
options: Both of them are good at painting and drawing
Neither of them plays any kind of music at all
Neil plays the piano well, but Sam can't draw
Sam plays the piano a bit; Neil can't paint
questions.why: Sam plays the piano a bit and feels quite artistic; Neil says 'basically no – I can't paint'.

questions.q: Which example does Neil give of an artist's strange behaviour?
options: Michelangelo worked so hard he never bathed
Mozart refused to play in front of the Emperor
Jimi Hendrix painted pictures on his guitar
Michelangelo slept in his studio for many years
questions.why: Neil says Michelangelo worked so hard he never took a bath, and Hendrix set fire to his guitar.

questions.q: What does Dr Rebecca Chamberlain measure in her research?
options: How long artists spend finishing each drawing
The quick jumps our eyes make between things
Which colours artists prefer to use in paintings
How much brain activity music creates in people
questions.why: She measures saccades – the rapid movements our eyes make as they jump from one thing to another.

questions.q: What did Rebecca find about how artists look at things when drawing?
options: They focus for a long time on the small details
They hardly move their eyes at all while drawing
They take in the whole picture with big eye jumps
They look at the image far less than non-artists do
questions.why: She says artists make bigger saccades and shorter fixations, taking a more global approach.

questions.q: What happened to one of Mike's students?
options: He couldn't draw, but was good within a month
He was already talented and became a famous painter
He gave up painting completely after a few lessons
He taught Mike a useful way to draw human faces
questions.why: Mike says the student 'could not draw – at all', but after some tips he was really good in a month.

questions.q: Why does Mike compare painting to riding a bike?
options: To show that painting can sometimes be dangerous
To explain that he likes to paint outdoors
To say that once you learn it you never forget it
To show it's a skill that people can learn
questions.why: He says some things are trainable, 'it's like a bike', meaning artistic ability can be learned.

questions.q: What third possibility do some scientists suggest?
options: Only child prodigies have truly artistic brains from birth
Every brain fills in the missing pieces its own way
Artistic ability comes only from many years of hard work
Artists' eyes are physically different from other people's
questions.why: Neil says every brain focuses on some areas and ignores others, and we fill in the missing pieces our own way.
